final_candidates.decision_summary: V38D has exceptionally poor fixed-backbone compatibility, near-zero sequence plausibility, and no observed Asp among well-covered homologs, strongly supporting folding disruption.
V36D is strongly incompatible with the experimental backbone and highly implausible by sequence and evolutionary evidence.
F60D combines poor structural compatibility with negligible sequence plausibility and evolutionary absence, making it a stronger unfolding candidate than the naturally tolerated F40D alternative.

stop_reason.detail: Multiple orthogonal evidence dimensions yield a stable Top-3 despite residual uncertainty about global unfolding versus localized disruption.

history.rationale: Replacing a bulky aromatic residue with an acidic residue may disrupt hydrophobic packing and introduce an unfavorable buried charge.

Although W17D is highly sequence-implausible and evolutionarily absent, its fixed-backbone compatibility is only mildly unfavorable. This weakens the case that it will reliably unfold PsaE rather than cause a localized perturbation.
This aromatic-to-acidic substitution is strongly nonconservative and may destabilize the compact fold.

The substitution is structurally disfavored, sequence-implausible, and absent from fully covered homologs. Its predicted structural incompatibility is nevertheless less extreme than for the leading valine substitutions.
Introducing aspartate at a hydrophobic isoleucine position may severely impair core packing and folding.

Asp is actually favored by ProteinMPNN on the fixed backbone and has substantial sequence-model plausibility. These signals strongly oppose the intended folding destabilization despite its absence from the limited homolog set.

rejection.reason: Asp is actually favored by ProteinMPNN on the fixed backbone and has substantial sequence-model plausibility. These signals strongly oppose the intended folding destabilization despite its absence from the limited homolog set.

history.rationale: Loss of an aromatic side chain combined with introduction of negative charge may create substantial local instability.

ProteinMPNN considers Asp highly compatible at position 34 despite its sequence-level implausibility. For a folding-disruption objective, this direct structural contradiction outweighs the indirect evolutionary signal.

rejection.reason: ProteinMPNN considers Asp highly compatible at position 34 despite its sequence-level implausibility. For a folding-disruption objective, this direct structural contradiction outweighs the indirect evolutionary signal.

history.rationale: A hydrophobic-to-charged substitution in the central PVIV segment is likely to disrupt packing if this region is structurally buried.
V36D is strongly incompatible with the experimental backbone and highly implausible to the sequence model. Its evolutionary absence is consistent with a damaging substitution.
Aspartate at this hydrophobic position may impose both packing defects and electrostatic strain, favoring unfolding.
Sequence and evolutionary evidence indicate an unusual substitution, but ProteinMPNN finds only moderate incompatibility. It is therefore less compelling as a direct folding-disruption design.
This nonconservative substitution may destabilize the hydrophobic cluster surrounding residues 33–40.

The exceptionally poor fixed-backbone compatibility and near-zero sequence plausibility strongly favor folding disruption. Absence of Asp among well-covered homologs provides additional, indirect support.
Replacing phenylalanine with aspartate removes a large aromatic packing group and may introduce a buried charge.

Structural and sequence-model evidence predicts substantial incompatibility, but Asp occurs in approximately 19% of aligned homologs. That natural occurrence lowers confidence that F40D consistently disrupts folding.
An aromatic-to-acidic change could disrupt local packing in the glycine-rich C-terminal half of the protein.

The mutation is comparatively compatible with the experimental backbone and has nonzero sequence plausibility. Evolutionary evidence has low positional coverage and does not rescue it as a folding-disruption candidate.

rejection.reason: The mutation is comparatively compatible with the experimental backbone and has nonzero sequence plausibility. Evolutionary evidence has low positional coverage and does not rescue it as a folding-disruption candidate.

history.rationale: Substitution of phenylalanine by aspartate may destabilize the C-terminal structural region through loss of hydrophobic packing.

F60D has poor backbone compatibility, negligible sequence plausibility, and no observed Asp among well-covered homologs. It remains a strong alternative, though its structural penalty is weaker than those of V38D and V36D.
